name: Pimoroni Badger 2350
description: 2.7 inch 264x176 four-grey e-paper badge (SSD1680) with an RP2350, Wi-Fi and five buttons. Runs the tesserae-device-badger app inside the stock Badgeware menu: it pairs over the REST device API, paints the dashboard in four greys and sends A/B/C/up/down as button wakes. The server sends a 2-bpp esp32_gray2_bin frame, which the app expands into Badgeware's RGBA screen buffer.
notes_md:
Client: [dmellok/tesserae-device-badger](https://github.com/dmellok/tesserae-device-badger), a Badgeware app. Double-tap RESET for the USB disk, copy the `tesserae` folder into `apps/`, add `TESSERAE_URL` to `secrets.py`, launch **Tesserae** from the menu, then click **Register** on the badge in Settings → Devices. Badgeware relaunches the app on every timer or button wake; press HOME to get back to the menu.

Buttons arrive with an action name and their own key: A `left`/`a`, B `refresh`/`b`, C `right`/`c`, up `left`/`up`, down `right`/`down`. The badge reports battery voltage, percentage and whether USB power is plugged in.

The frame is 11616 bytes (264*176/4), `0b00` black to `0b11` white. The SSD1680 driver keeps the top two bits of each pixel, so the levels land on 0x00, 0x40, 0x80 and 0xFF. The stay-awake and button-wake-window options don't apply.

Confirmed on a Badger 2350 running Badgeware 1.27.0: pairing, painting and the buttons. On that firmware only the full refresh drives the four greys, which the app uses for every frame. Whether the four codes form an even black-to-white ramp is still to be checked by eye.
